You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

To get **frequent museum visitors**, we need a definition of “frequent” (e.g., **at least N visits**, or **top K by number of visits**). Here are common options you can use.

### 1) Visitors with at least N visits (replace `N`)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= N
ORDER BY num_visits DESC, v.Name;
```

### 2) Top K most frequent visitors (replace `K`)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
ORDER BY num_visits DESC
LIMIT K;
```

### 3) Frequent visitors per museum (at least N visits to the same museum)
```sql
SELECT
  m.Museum_ID,
  m.Name AS museum_name,
  v.ID AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits_to_museum
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
JOIN museum m ON m.Museum_ID = vi.Museum_ID
GROUP BY m.Museum_ID, m.Name, v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= N
ORDER BY m.Museum_ID, num_visits_to_museum DESC;
```

Which definition do you want: **at least N visits**, **top K**, and is it **overall** or **per museum**?
I'm thinking of the ones who go multiple times to museums.

```sql
-- Visitors who visited museums multiple times (2+ total visits)
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY total_visits DESC, v.Name;
```

If you meant “multiple times to the same museum” instead, tell me and I’ll adjust it.
focus on the people who visit museums.

```sql
-- People who have visited at least one museum
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID,
  v.Name
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
ORDER BY v.Name;
```
I want to focus on the visitors for museums. Get their unique IDs too.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  vi.visitor_ID AS visitor_id
FROM visit vi
ORDER BY vi.visitor_ID;
```
I want to focus on the visitors to museums specifically.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID   AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v
  ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
also need to get their names

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID   AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v
  ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
I also need to get their ages along with the other details.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID   AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Age  AS age
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v
  ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
